source_user: Calculation case 295: a model has 56 layers, 6 KV heads, head dimension 64, sequence length 1024, and INT8 KV values. Estimate bytes for one request's K/V cache. Show the formula and report GiB.
source_assistant: Use 2 × layers × sequence_length × KV_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_value. Here this is 2 × 56 × 1024 × 6 × 64 × 1 = 44040192 bytes = 0.041016 GiB. This excludes allocator metadata and other runtime memory.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions that must be checked against config.json and the serving engine before this number drives a capacity decision: (1) standard attention with exactly one K tensor and one V tensor per layer — this is the source of the leading factor of 2; (2) the head count used is num_key_value_heads (GQA/MQA), not num_attention_heads; (3) no sliding-window attention, no cross-attention KV, and no MLA-style latent KV compression — each breaks linearity in sequence length, sliding-window by capping effective S at the window, MLA by storing a compressed latent instead of full K/V; (4) sequence length means total context (prompt + generated tokens), not prompt alone.

Formula: kv_bytes = 2 (K and V) x num_layers x seq_len x num_kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_value.

Substituting: 2 x 56 x 1024 x 6 x 64 x 1 = 44040192 bytes = 42.0000 MiB = 0.041016 GiB (GiB = bytes / 2^30). Dtype assumed: INT8 (1 byte/value). Per-token KV cost is 2 x 56 x 6 x 64 x 1 = 43008 bytes/token, which is the number to use for admission control and for extrapolating to other context lengths.

Case-specific notes:
- num_kv_heads = 6 is a hard tensor-parallel divisibility constraint: TP must divide 6 for KV to shard cleanly. When TP > num_kv_heads the engine replicates KV per rank, so aggregate KV grows linearly with TP and per-GPU KV stops shrinking — the usual reason a 'more GPUs' plan fails to buy more context.
- Depth-dominated case (56 layers): KV is linear in layer count, so KV-dtype quantization at best halves the term; only reducing max context or per-request concurrency changes the shape of the curve.
- Short context (1024 tokens): at this size fixed overheads — CUDA graph pools, activation workspace, allocator fragmentation — are comparable to or larger than the 42.00 MiB of KV, so single-request KV is a poor predictor of total per-request memory.
- INT8 KV: 1 byte/value is payload only. Per-group scale (and zero-point if asymmetric) adds roughly 2/g bytes per value — about 12.5% at group size 16, about 1.6% at 128, doubled for asymmetric quantization. INT8 KV is also an accuracy-affecting change and must pass a task-level quality gate, not just a memory gate.

- PagedAttention block rounding: allocation is ceil(seq_len/B_blk) x B_blk tokens, so short or ragged requests waste up to (B_blk - 1) tokens of KV each.
- Prefix caching / radix-tree reuse keeps blocks resident after a request completes, so steady-state KV exceeds the sum of live requests.
- Speculative decoding and beam search hold KV for draft or branch tokens that may be discarded, multiplying the figure by the branch factor at peak.
- Engines preallocate a KV pool at startup (e.g. gpu_memory_utilization), so nvidia-smi shows pool size, not live KV occupancy; the two must not be compared directly.

source_user: Calculation case 303: a model has 40 layers, 6 KV heads, head dimension 128, sequence length 1536, and BF16/FP16 KV values. Estimate bytes for one request's K/V cache. Show the formula and report GiB.
source_assistant: Use 2 × layers × sequence_length × KV_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_value. Here this is 2 × 40 × 1536 × 6 × 128 × 2 = 188743680 bytes = 0.175781 GiB. This excludes allocator metadata and other runtime memory.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions that must be checked against config.json and the serving engine before this number drives a capacity decision: (1) standard attention with exactly one K tensor and one V tensor per layer — this is the source of the leading factor of 2; (2) the head count used is num_key_value_heads (GQA/MQA), not num_attention_heads; (3) no sliding-window attention, no cross-attention KV, and no MLA-style latent KV compression — each breaks linearity in sequence length, sliding-window by capping effective S at the window, MLA by storing a compressed latent instead of full K/V; (4) sequence length means total context (prompt + generated tokens), not prompt alone.

Formula: kv_bytes = 2 (K and V) x num_layers x seq_len x num_kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_value.

Substituting: 2 x 40 x 1536 x 6 x 128 x 2 = 188743680 bytes = 180.0000 MiB = 0.175781 GiB (GiB = bytes / 2^30). Dtype assumed: BF16/FP16 (2 bytes/value). Per-token KV cost is 2 x 40 x 6 x 128 x 2 = 122880 bytes/token, which is the number to use for admission control and for extrapolating to other context lengths.

Case-specific notes:
- num_kv_heads = 6 is a hard tensor-parallel divisibility constraint: TP must divide 6 for KV to shard cleanly. When TP > num_kv_heads the engine replicates KV per rank, so aggregate KV grows linearly with TP and per-GPU KV stops shrinking — the usual reason a 'more GPUs' plan fails to buy more context.
- Short context (1536 tokens): at this size fixed overheads — CUDA graph pools, activation workspace, allocator fragmentation — are comparable to or larger than the 180.00 MiB of KV, so single-request KV is a poor predictor of total per-request memory.

Boundary conditions the raw figure does not capture, each pushing real allocation upward:
- PagedAttention block rounding: allocation is ceil(seq_len/B_blk) x B_blk tokens, so short or ragged requests waste up to (B_blk - 1) tokens of KV each.
- Prefix caching / radix-tree reuse keeps blocks resident after a request completes, so steady-state KV exceeds the sum of live requests.
- Speculative decoding and beam search hold KV for draft or branch tokens that may be discarded, multiplying the figure by the branch factor at peak.
- Engines preallocate a KV pool at startup (e.g. gpu_memory_utilization), so nvidia-smi shows pool size, not live KV occupancy; the two must not be compared directly.
- In disaggregated prefill/decode or KV-offload designs (Mooncake-style pooled KV store, NVIDIA Dynamo KV-aware routing), this same byte count becomes a network transfer: at a 200 Gb/s RoCE line rate, 188743680 bytes needs at least 7.550 ms of wire time per request, excluding RDMA setup, GDS/GDR staging and congestion; that floor is a hard lower bound on any TTFT budget that includes a KV migration.

Falsifiable test: run the engine with max_num_seqs=1 and a single request of exactly this context length, read the engine's own reported KV cache size (vLLM logs num_gpu_blocks x block_size x per-token KV bytes), and compare with the 122880 bytes/token derived above. Deviation beyond roughly 10% falsifies one of the four assumptions — most often head_dim padding, an MLA/sliding-window layer mix, or num_attention_heads used in place of num_key_value_heads.

Rollback gate: if after acting on this estimate the deployment shows a preemption/swap rate above 1%, a p99 TTFT regression above 20% versus the prior configuration, or any CUDA OOM in engine logs, revert the context/concurrency change and re-measure with the single-request test before retrying.
risks: Arithmetic is correct but the answer omits the assumptions it depends on (GQA kv-head count, no MLA/sliding-window, total context), so it silently breaks on modern architectures.
No mention of PagedAttention block rounding, prefix-cache retention, or speculative/beam KV, so the figure underestimates steady-state footprint if used for capacity planning.
No falsifiable verification step and no rollback gate, so an operator could size a production KV pool on an unvalidated analytic number.
